label: late original positions / <DEL> in long sequences beginning n-p.. (diffuse prefix-combination feature)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.06% of steps) that fires only at the last few original-phase steps (orig_idx 5-8, peaking at 6-7) and at the <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7). It never fires in the copy phase or at t<4. Inside that window, whether it fires depends on a diffuse combination of earlier tokens: first token n gives 13x lift and 52% of the mass, p at position 1 or 2 and the digit 2 at position 1 raise it further, and current input u (6.6x) and previous input s (7.8x) are also enriched. The strongest activations come from sequences like n p k q p s u. No compact predicate captures this. The window condition alone has ~99% recall but 0.3% precision, and the best conjunction (n first, then p or 2 early) reaches only about 0.22 F1 on dev. The feature looks like a hidden-state code for a specific family of prefixes, read out near the end of the input.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+6.51), orig2=p (+5.15), orig1=p (+4.57), orig2=k (+4.30), orig0=o (+4.22), prev_tok=s (+3.75). Lower it: phase=2 (-5.80), prev3_tok=- (-5.55), t=3 (-4.26), t=4 (-3.75).
